![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132962/assets/2197dd68c567a5232ddf850b7ff8972033eb8cd0d11980baf6dc8e0a198b00a9.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $x$-axis and the curves $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt{2-x}$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=12y,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,y\le x\le 2-{y}^{2},\,\,0\le y\le 1\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132962/assets/7a4216a2b1dc3859776c6589459d687981b79b123fa3a5eea638d31529e5cd3a.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-{y}^{2}}{y}^{2}\cdot 12y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{y}^{2-{y}^{2}}12{y}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[12x{y}^{3}]_{x=y}^{x=2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}12(2-{y}^{2}){y}^{3}-12{y}^{4}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}24{y}^{3}-12{y}^{5}-12{y}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[6{y}^{4}-2{y}^{6}-\frac{12}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =6-2-\frac{12}{5} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
